title: A nickname that looks like one letter can be 161 code points long
assumption: A short-looking string is a short string, so a per-character length limit also bounds how much text it can contain.

input.display: "e" followed by a combining mark repeated 20 times ("\u0301\u0310\u0327\u032d\u0353\u0338\u035f\u0360" x 20) — "Zalgo text"
input.description: A display name, comment, or review submitted with Unicode combining marks stacked onto a single base character (easy to generate with any "Zalgo text" web tool), occupying one visual line position but arbitrarily many code points.

what_goes_wrong: The string occupies roughly one glyph's space (an "e" under a stack of marks) but is 161 code points and 321 UTF-8 bytes. A "nickname must be 1-20 characters" validator that counts grapheme clusters, the measure usually recommended for user-facing length, counts it as 1 character and accepts it, while it takes far more storage than any 20-character name and can render as a tall smear over neighbouring lines.
why: Unicode's definition of well-formed text puts no limit on how many combining marks (General Category Mn, Mc, Me) may follow one base character. Each mark is a legal code point that stacks on the previous one, and UAX #29 groups the base and all of its marks into a single grapheme cluster, so a grapheme count sees one character however many marks follow. UAX #15 defines a "Stream-Safe Text Format" that caps runs of non-starters at 30, but it is a recommendation that nothing enforces by default. Code-point or byte limits catch this particular string, which is why the fix combines both measures.

repros.code:
base = "e"
marks = "\u0301\u0310\u0327\u032d\u0353\u0338\u035f\u0360"
zalgo = base + marks * 20
print(len(zalgo), len(zalgo.encode("utf-8")))

fix: Enforce a limit in code points or bytes for storage as well as a grapheme-cluster limit for what the user sees, and cap the number of combining marks per base character (a handful covers real orthographies; UAX #15's Stream-Safe Text Format uses 30 as an upper bound).
